indicators.note: inside tells us the article sits within the word for story

parts.note: a newspaper story is copy
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A journalist covers a story that contains a particular article.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy is an overhead covering, such as over a bed or a throne.

definitions.meaning: bearing as in how one holds oneself, posture
the fee charged for conveying goods

explanation.surface: A remark about who pays the freight charges.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage means one's posture or deportment, and also the charge made for conveying goods.

indicators.note: turn out suggests the letters are turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A seaman going mad is evicted from his ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn out' rearranges the letters of A LUNATIC; 'marine' is the adjective meaning of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical and marine are both adjectives describing things relating to the sea or sailors.

clue.text: One may find their pulse worth taking

definitions.text: One may find their pulse worth taking

parts.words: One may find their pulse worth taking
parts.note: pulse here is peas and beans, the edible seeds held in these seed cases, not a heartbeat

explanation.surface: A doctor deciding whether to check patients' heart rates.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea and bean seeds, called pulses, grow inside long seed cases on the plant.

clue.text: Grey is to study Maugham's work

parts.note: ashen means pale grey
a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to read Somerset Maugham's writing in grey surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset Maugham wrote a book of spy stories with this title, named after its secret-agent hero.

clue.text: One who is out and about

definitions.text: One who is out and about

parts.words: One who is out and about
parts.note: out here means asleep, so this is someone wandering about while unconscious

explanation.surface: A description of someone sociable who gets around a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleepwalker moves around the house while fast asleep, so is both out cold and up and about.

parts.note: losing one's heart means falling in love, which is what the arrows of the Greek love god do

explanation.surface: A villain whose victims become discouraged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love shoots arrows that make people fall for someone.

clue.text: The cad is out to break the engagement

indicators.note: is out suggests these letters are in disarray and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rotter is gone, leaving the fiancee to call off the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out' scrambles THE CAD; 'engagement' is meant mechanically, like gears meshing, not a betrothal.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate one part from another is to disengage it, ending its connection.

definitions.meaning: British slang for irritated or fed up
a nark is a police informer, and to nark is to tell tales to them

explanation.surface: Someone irritated enough to report a neighbour to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: This British slang word means irritated, and is also the past tense of a verb for acting as a police informer.

definitions.meaning: a session of golf or a period of a boxing match

explanation.surface: A query about the social groups who play golf or box.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer plays eighteen holes per session and a boxing bout has three-minute sessions, each so named; circles are also so named, as ring shapes.

clue.text: Phoney admission of poverty takes in a good man

indicators.note: takes in means the admission surrounds the other piece

parts.note: someone admitting poverty says I'm poor
ST is short for saint, a good man

explanation.surface: A fake confesses to being poor while sheltering a virtuous man.
explanation.definitionFit: A phoney is a fraud, someone pretending to be another person.

clue.text: Private eye in disguise, quite angry

indicators.note: a disguise alters appearance, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A detective working undercover is rather cross.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' of 'in disguise' is part of the fodder: IN plus QUITE ANGRY make the twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old-fashioned British term for a private detective.

definitions.meaning: flag is another name for the plant, especially the yellow wild variety
the Greek rainbow goddess, or the coloured part of the eye

explanation.surface: A description of a multicoloured banner.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow flag is a wild species of this plant, and the Greek goddess of the rainbow had this name.

clue.text: Turn can up to take top off

indicators.note: turn tells us to turn these letters around into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions for opening a tin by turning it upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove a lid or cap is to take off its top.

parts.note: AC is alternating current
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man's present longing.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache can be a yearning or longing for something.

clue.text: Charm, going topless at fashionable race meeting

indicators.note: losing its top means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: a mascot is a lucky charm

explanation.surface: A lucky charm worn by someone going topless at a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a racecourse in Berkshire whose Royal meeting is a high point of the British social season.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal meeting at this Berkshire racecourse is famous for its fashion and hats.

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
ease means comfort or relief

explanation.surface: An order to stop offering cold comfort to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt is to come to an end, desist.

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old sailor complains about his ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' (an old sailor) and 'vessel' paint a nautical scene, but the vessel is a drinking glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking glass with a flat bottom and no stem is a container, a vessel for liquid.

clue.text: About five, porter has time for a drink

indicators.note: about means the beer goes around the number

parts.note: porter is a dark beer
V is the Roman numeral for five
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Around five o'clock, a hotel porter finds time for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' looks like a hotel worker, but it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Any liquid for drinking, other than water, is called this.

indicators.note: organising means putting the letters into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone arranges Sue's opal wedding anniversary.
explanation.definitionFit: Espousal is a formal word for marriage or a betrothal ceremony.

parts.note: a quartet is four
shamefaced people go red, so are ones who flush

explanation.surface: Four people embarrassed at having been caught cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: A four-flush is a poker bluff with four cards of a suit posing as a flush, hence the American term for bluffers.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for bluffers or cheats, from poker players pretending to hold a full flush.

clue.text: He takes orders to break the circle

indicators.note: break the word means smash it up and rearrange its letters

explanation.surface: A man follows instructions to break out of a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes orders' suggests obedience, but means being ordained into the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest is ordained, entering holy orders.

parts.note: read literally, this is the outlet through which the smoke of a ship's furnace escapes

explanation.surface: A description of an emergency exit on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamship's chimney carries smoke from the boiler fires up and away.

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: dual means double

explanation.surface: Ordering a double round of drinks to celebrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a round of drinks, but it turns DUAL back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone highly is to extol them.

parts.note: a lass is a girl
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone trying to win a girl who has nothing to her.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's looped rope is used to capture cattle.

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A woman's beloved was the young man of Greek legend.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek legend Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his lover, a priestess of Aphrodite; the whole clue tells their story.
explanation.definitionFit: The priestess in the legend was the woman Leander loved and swam to each night.

parts.note: to notice is to see
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Spotting a crowd appearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To look or give the impression of being something.

definitions.meaning: a sea fish of the perch family
low in pitch, as a voice or note

explanation.surface: A fish living deep in a strait or inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sea fish, and also the term for the lowest range of musical pitch.

definitions.meaning: handed in, as an account or bill
covered a wall with a facing coat of plaster

explanation.surface: Someone surrendered and was made to stand against the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: It means handed over or delivered, and also coated with a layer of plaster.

clue.text: Harry can be just as rash if upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Harry behaves impulsively when he is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name, but it is the verb meaning to pester; 'upset' rearranges AS RASH.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to pester or torment repeatedly.

clue.text: A strike in the town would be a catastrophe

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: a city is a large town
lam is to strike or thrash

explanation.surface: Industrial action in a town would be a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action, but it is LAM, to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is an event causing great damage or distress.

parts.note: a swell is a grand or important person

explanation.surface: A very important person as well.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means also, in addition.
